name: Example: Finding a Matrix that Defines an Orthogonal Projection Onto the Subspace Spanned by a Vector
problem: Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of $\mathbb{R}^3$ onto the subspace spanned by ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071876/assets/16f06043e1f8bcab11a7e43fc76800c33e2560bb00e425c9c88f8cfeb8c12ee3.png)
worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix $P_S = A(A^T\!A)^{-1}\!A^T$ maps any vector $\mathbf x\in \mathbb{R}^n$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

In our case, ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071876/assets/fde70db50cff408347bdebc086fbfa3ae87020bb0300b32dad67168d617ed607.png) Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]\cdot (14)^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{14}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{14}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 \\ 2 & 4 & -6 \\ -3 & -6 & 9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
